exceptions.reason: Placement: a phone on its side hides the drawer's brand (the top bar under the scrim has it) so the session list keeps its height.
Placement: on a phone in portrait and on its side the brand gives its width to the session's name; Home is the drawer's first item.

Placement: on a phone every page's bar shows the mark without its name; DS lets the name give way only beside a .ds-topbar__title, which these bars do not have (the session's name is a rename button).

Placement: a phone on its side with its keyboard up leaves a strip, and the bar steps aside whatever has the focus; DS's .ds-app--keyboard-hides-bar waits for html[data-ds-keyboard], which DS.dom.followViewport (2.1) sets for a field in VS Code's frame but not for its editor in Chromium, an EditContext element that is neither a textarea nor contenteditable.
Wrapping: the Status modal's figures are spans in words ("Your turn"), wider than a third of the 600px modal at the figure's size; they take a second line between words instead of DS's ellipsis.
Layout: the figures of a row of Home's tiles stand on one line however many lines a label takes.
Wrapping: a long label breaks inside a word rather than run past a 320px tile.
Wrapping: a tile's note is one line with an ellipsis (its tip has the whole), and on a phone it gives way, so the rows of tiles keep one height.
Wrapping: the answer's words are the person's, a path among them; they break anywhere rather than widen the card.

Spacing: a card head holds a status chip, which DS (2.1) sits on the title's line; a chip that wraps under a long title stands a chip's gap under it, not the larger row gap DS keeps for a button that hangs out of the line.
Layout: the answer's chip and its words read as one line, not as two ends of the row; its words are a meta line, which DS hangs out of the line like a button, onto the chip when a long answer wraps.
Layout: the schedule field's label carries a clock glyph beside its words.
Wrapping: a closed filter cuts a long account or project with an ellipsis; its tip says it whole.
Wrapping: a model's description and a folder's path under its name in the open list are read to their end.
Wrapping: a hint quoting a preset's bare path breaks anywhere rather than run out of the sheet.
